reason: Both before bodies repeat the loaded-module guard, import and class-membership predicate. The commit replaces that repeated core with _issubclass_fast(type(x), module, class), retaining NumPy/Jax zero-gradient specialization. This is a real parameterized helper extraction, NOT evidence that one backend predicate can call another unchanged. All 21 pairs are ONE correlated refactor family in vendored MIT-licensed code (array_api_compat/LICENSE).

The two functions duplicate recipient validation, EmailMultiAlternatives construction, HTML attachment and sending; ADMINS versus MANAGERS is the configuration difference. The commit extracts _send_server_message(setting_name=...) and both wrappers call it. Calling mail_managers from mail_admins unchanged would send to the wrong recipients, so this is helper-extraction evidence, not direct-call equivalence.

Both before implementations copy self, set is_summary and resolve child expressions. The commit moves Func's composite-expression validation into BaseExpression and deletes Func's override, inheriting the generalized implementation. This is an author-performed consolidation, but before-state BaseExpression lacks Func's validation: direct replacement without extending it would be unsafe.

Both before helpers validate one captured record, its message and status. The commit extends assertLogRecord with level/request checks and a return value, makes LogResponseRealLoggerTests inherit the mixin and replaces every assertResponseLogged call. Real duplicate assertion logic is consolidated; the old target alone lacks checks and a return value, so it is not a safe unchanged replacement. Test-only evidence, outside the production skipTests population.
